newsitem.title: GREECE: DEBT RESTRUCTURING PENSION FUND OFFER DRAWS LITTLE INTEREST - ANA.
newsitem.headline: DEBT RESTRUCTURING PENSION FUND OFFER DRAWS LITTLE INTEREST - ANA.

text.p: The debt restructuring offer extended by the Greek labour ministry to those with overdue debts to pension funds was a limited success, state Athens News Agency said.
Only 44,000 out of 217,000 debtors of IKA pension fund took the offer and IKA is expected to collect 97 billion drachmas out of 327 billion owed, it said.
IKA will also collect just 56.7 billion drachmas out of 260 billion in penalties.
TEVE pension fund saw 35 percent of its debtors take the restructuring offer and the fund will collect 20 billion drachmas out of the 50 or 60 billion owed.
Overdue debts to pension funds are estimated by the minsitry to over 600 billion drachmas.
